title: Improving AI Discernment: do misinformation interventions help people spot AI-generated media?

registration.note: AsPredicted #151,281, registered 2023-11-15 (amends #151208). Some data had been collected at registration; batches 3-4 followed the plan.

descriptions.0: No intervention; the respondent proceeds directly to the discernment task.
descriptions.1: Posts in the feed are flagged as potentially AI-generated.
descriptions.2: Posts carry information about the content's source and origin (provenance).
descriptions.3: Posts carry machine-learning-based AI-detection labels (automated flagging).
descriptions.4: Before the feed, an interactive task asks 'Is this image AI-generated?' (accuracy nudge).
descriptions.5: Before the feed, a box-breathing exercise to reduce emotional reactivity.
descriptions.6: Before the feed, a short mindfulness exercise.
descriptions.7: Before the feed, an inoculation message pre-exposing the respondent to manipulation techniques used in AI-generated media.
descriptions.8: Before the feed, an infographic on how to identify AI-generated content.
descriptions.9: Before the feed, an alternative infographic on how to identify AI-generated content.
descriptions.10: Before the feed, a comprehensive guide with examples of AI artifacts in images and videos.
descriptions.11: Before the feed, an educational video about AI-generated text.

derived.ai_scale: (chatgpt + bing + claude + character + dalle + midjourney + stable_diff) / 7

addenda.label: exclude low political-knowledge respondents (pk_score<1), full estimates and CIs
addenda.rationale: The reviewer notes the exclusion is a low-knowledge screen, not an attention check, so it should be labelled that way and reported with estimates, SEs and CIs. This re-runs H1 excluding pk_score<1, so readers can see whether effects shrink or just get noisier.
addenda.expected: Point estimates similar to the registered analysis with wider CIs would suggest lost precision, not a vanished effect. Sign changes or large shifts in estimates would worry a reader.
addenda.issue: The E1 table has empty est/se/p columns for every arm, yet the text claims that Automated Flagging (p=0.004) and AI Literacy Guide (p=0.043) became nonsignificant. Nothing displayed supports this. The 'attention-check failure' label is also misleading: pk_score<1 is a knowledge-question failure, not an attention check, and may be post-treatment-correlated or confounded with ability. Dropping 30% of the sample is not a clean robustness test.

addenda.label: unadjusted difference in means, no covariates, same weights
addenda.rationale: Reviewer suspects the Lin interaction model and covariate leverage drive the heterogeneous arm SEs (e.g., Breathing Exercise). Re-fitting without covariates shows whether arm estimates, SEs and the pooled effect hold up without covariate adjustment.
addenda.expected: Similar arm estimates and more uniform SEs, with a pooled effect near -0.11, would reassure; large shifts in SEs or estimates would point to covariate leverage or outliers in the Lin model.
addenda.issue: The text says the other ten arms had estimates 'between −0.16 and 0.00', but the pooled random-effects result (−0.11, p=0.026) is reported as significant and tied to nothing in the narrative. The Breathing Exercise result (−0.54) has an SE of 0.23 that is much larger than the other arms' SEs, and arm-level SEs vary oddly (0.116 to 0.280), which suggests the Lin interaction model or outliers are driving them.
